lesson.summary: AWS offers purpose-built compute services for specific needs. AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys and scales web applications while AWS handles the provisioning, load balancing and health monitoring. AWS Batch runs large sets of batch jobs and scales resources to match. Amazon Lightsail gives simple virtual servers at a predictable monthly price. AWS Outposts runs AWS infrastructure and services inside your own data center for hybrid setups.
keyPoints: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a managed service: you upload your code and it handles provisioning, scaling, load balancing and health monitoring
AWS Batch schedules and scales compute resources for batch jobs, which suits large parallel workloads such as simulations or media transcoding
Amazon Lightsail provides virtual private servers, storage, databases and networking at a predictable monthly price for simple workloads
AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure and services to your on-premises data center for low-latency or data residency needs
Choose the service that matches the workload: web application, batch processing, simple website or on-premises hybrid

scenarios.text: A pharmaceutical research company runs thousands of compute-heavy simulations. The jobs run in parallel, do not need real-time interaction, and the company wants them scheduled and scaled automatically based on computing demand.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service best fits this workload?
questions.explanation: AWS Batch schedules and scales compute for batch jobs that run in parallel. Lightsail suits simple websites, Elastic Beanstalk deploys web applications, and Outposts runs AWS in your own data center.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to deploy a web application without managing the provisioning, load balancing and health monitoring. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk takes your code and handles provisioning, scaling, load balancing and health monitoring. Batch is for batch jobs, Outposts is hybrid infrastructure, and Lightsail is for simple servers.

questions.prompt: A freelancer wants a simple blog with storage and compute in one package at a predictable monthly price. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Lightsail provides virtual private servers, storage and networking at a predictable monthly price, which suits simple sites. Outposts is for hybrid data centers, Batch is for batch jobs, and Fargate is serverless compute for containers.

questions.prompt: A company needs AWS services running in its own data center because of low latency and data residency rules. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Outposts extends AWS infrastructure and services into your on-premises data center, which suits low-latency and data residency needs.

questions.prompt: Match each service with its main purpose.

pairs.right: Deploys and scales web applications from uploaded code
Schedules and scales large batch jobs
Simple virtual servers at a predictable monthly price
AWS infrastructure inside your on-premises data center

questions.explanation: Each service targets a different need: web application deployment, batch processing, simple predictable hosting, and hybrid on-premises infrastructure.
